short: LipNet decoder on rtMRI (M06) and sentence-text output (M08) are standard; one split, no repeats (M12, behind); USC-TIMIT's shared 460-sentence list likely puts training sentences in the test.
position: The paper moves the LipNet decoder onto USC-TIMIT real-time MRI (M06) and makes sentence text the output of a vocal-tract MRI decoder (M08). Both are standard: the 3D-convolution front end is the field's most common articulator-video design, and the text output, unique among 88 vocal-tract MRI studies, follows HMM sequence recognition of continuous rtMRI speech (Katsamanis et al., 2011) and rests on one speaker-held-out split. The evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work, which repeated splits or folds. The strongest confound is the closed sentence list: every USC-TIMIT speaker reads the same 460 sentences, so the 40.6% PER most likely measures speaker transfer on a closed list, not open sentence recognition (inference). The title overreaches: the speech is audible, and no emotion is recognized; the emotion analysis averages a deviation measure over two words without a test.
